svg.title: Smart Cities SIG at a glance
svg.desc: The problem cities face (too many standards and devices, data without context, manual adaptation and vendor lock-in); what the SIG is (open, implementation-neutral, not a standards body); its goal (the city's needs drive the data, not the device); the four stages from Operational Meaning to Smart Data Models Realization, ending in a Smart City Profile, with a Proof of Concept in 2027; and where it stands in October 2026, with the Smart City Expo World Congress in Barcelona as the next milestone.
svg.text: Smart Cities SIG at a glance
Open, implementation-neutral collaboration on smart city interoperability · since May 2026
Cities face many IoT standards and devices
Data reaches the Digital Twin without what was
measured, where, how, and how far to trust it.
Each city adapts the data by hand, and
Open, implementation-neutral, and not a standards body
It analyzes real municipal needs and feeds its findings back to the organizations
that own the specifications: OMA, FIWARE / Smart Data Models, and others.

text.tspan: The goal: the city's needs drive the data, not the device.
For each Service Domain, a Smart City Profile that any city can adopt.

svg.text: One per Service Domain, for any city
The OMA objects that feed them
Stages 2 and 3: the capability taxonomy, the municipality questions,
and the OMA and Smart Data Models assessments.
After that: the Smart City Profiles
